summary: Coos FPA lookout site on an Aircraft Warning Service post (1942); several rebuilds and a 1996 wind collapse; present 40-ft steel tower unstaffed with a camera, not public.

facts.design: 40-foot all-steel tower with a 6-by-6-foot cab (present structure)

access.note: Cheryl Hill's Oregon list marks the site as not accessible to the public. The list gives no reason.

events.note: Activated as an Aircraft Warning Service post, September 12, 1942
20-foot timber tower with a 14x14 cabin replaced the old building. Forest Lookouts gives 1955 for this tower in another passage.
Fire six miles northeast of Langlois; the lookout station was evacuated and saved
Summer lookout assignment announced for the station
20-foot tower replaced by a 52-foot CT3 tower with a 14x14 cabin (Forest Lookouts). Firelookout.com says the 1974 tower blew over the following winter.
A November 1975 windstorm blew the tower down (Forest Lookouts). Firelookout.com gives a 53-foot tower built in 1975.
52-foot tower rebuilt; paid from the State Restoration Fund ($12,010)
High winds caused the tower to collapse on December 31, 1996
A new steel tower with a steel cab (Forest Lookouts). Firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill date the present tower to 2008.
Present 40-ft all-steel tower with a 6x6 cab; a trailer lookout was used until it was built
Coos FPA installed a smoke detection camera system; the tower is no longer staffed

corrections.why: Firelookout.com describes the present structure as a 40-foot tower. 1.8 m matches no tower height in the sources read.
Firelookout.com describes the present 40-foot tower as all-steel. The wood towers were the earlier timber structures.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com dates the first timber tower to 1951 after the 1942 AWS post. Forest Lookouts gives a 14-foot tower around 1941 and dates the 20-foot tower to 1955 in one passage and 1951 in another. We report the 1951 date that both sources share.
Curry County per firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts list; Coos County per the FFLA Oregon list, which the record used. Needs an editor check.
2008 per firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill; 1999 per Forest Lookouts.
52 feet per Forest Lookouts; 53 feet per firelookout.com for the 1975 tower.

notes_for_editor: Tower history conflicts across all four sources: first build year, 1974 and 1975 tower heights, the present tower's date (1999 vs 2008), and the county (Curry vs Coos). The record's height (1.8 m) and material (wood) look wrong for the present steel tower. Access is the Cheryl Hill column, which gives no reason for 'No'. No visiting information was found. The site was not checked against NHLR or FFLOS registers.
